parsed.title: SPEC Phases section has 9 phases, violating the ≤8 rule
parsed.detail: The SPEC's `## Phases` section lists P1 through P9. The `### Phase-lint` block at the top claims every phase passes the 8-box lint, but the Rules section states 'Skills stay within their context budgets' and the Phase-lint contract (referenced in P1-P8) enforces a maximum of 8 tasks/phases per phase block. More critically, the SPEC itself defines the Phase-lint rule as 'Every implementation phase below must pass all 8 boxes before it is emitted'. While P9 is 'Hardening & PR', the presence of 9 distinct phase blocks (P1-P9) in the execution ledger contradicts the structural constraint that phases are linted individually against the 8-box rule, and the SPEC's own `### Phase-lint` block lists 8 fingerprints (P1-P8) but the execution ledger below lists P1-P9. The SPEC's `### Phases` section lists P1..P8 in the lint block, but the actual phases listed below are P1..P9. The lint block only covers P1-P8. P9 is missing from the lint block, meaning it was not linted, violating the rule 'Every implementation phase below must pass all 8 boxes before it is emitted'.

parsed.title: Progress log lists P9 but SPEC lint block only covers P1-P8
parsed.detail: The `progress.md` file lists phases P1 through P9. The SPEC's `### Phase-lint` block (line 655 in SPEC.md) only records fingerprints for P1 through P8. The rule in the SPEC states 'Every implementation phase below must pass all 8 boxes before it is emitted'. P9 is an implementation phase (Hardening & PR) but lacks a lint record, meaning it was not verified as compliant with the 8-box rule before emission.

parsed.title: Router command generation for fix units uses unit.number but plan-fix expects issue number
parsed.detail: In the `main` function, for a fix unit, the command is set to `/plan-fix ${unit.number}`. However, `plan-fix`'s argument hint is `<issue-number> [<issue-number> …]`. The router resolves units from `docs/fix` folders named like `20-pending-topic` where `20` is the issue number. This seems correct. However, for feature units, it uses `unit.slug` (`/plan-feature ${unit.slug}`). The router's `resolveUnit` function extracts the number and slug from the folder name. For fix units, the folder is `docs/fix/<number>-<slug>`. The router uses `unit.number` for fix units. This is consistent. No defect here.

parsed.title: Router command for fix units uses unit.number, but plan-fix expects issue number
parsed.detail: The router generates `/plan-fix ${unit.number}` for fix units. The `plan-fix` skill expects an issue number. The fix unit folder is `docs/fix/<number>-<slug>`. The number is the issue number. This is correct. No defect.

parsed.title: Router command for fix units uses unit.number, but plan-fix expects issue number
parsed.detail: The router generates `/plan-fix ${unit.number}` for fix units. The `plan-fix` skill expects an issue number. The fix unit folder is `docs/fix/<number>-<slug>`. The number is the issue number. This is correct. No defect.
